sentences.text: Dinichthys was an extinct genus of large marine arthrodire placoderm fish that lived during the Late Devonian in Ohio and Tennessee, USA. This armored fish measured approximately 3 meters in length.
It was comparable in size, shape, and ecological role to the well-known Dunkleosteus.
Many illustrations supposedly representing Dinichthys are actually images of Dunkleosteus.
Fossils of Dinichthys were recovered from the Ohio Shale Formation near the Olentangy River in Delaware County, Ohio.
The species was originally described in 1868 by John Newberry based on an incomplete skull roof and mandibles.
A 2010 phylogenetic study found that Dinichthys and Dunkleosteus belong to two separate clades.
The family Dinichthyidae is now considered monospecific, containing only the genus Dinichthys and its type species D. herzeri.
Dinichthys lived from the Givetian to the Famennian stages, between 387.95 and 358.86 million years ago.
